subject.title: backup create stalls on large installations (4GB+ .openclaw dir)

question: What restore-safe core behavior should `openclaw backup create` support for large state directories: native smart/custom exclusions, a minimal completion/error/progress fix, or a documented coarse-backup boundary?
rationale: The bug is credible, but deciding default exclusions, protected backup contents, and whether scope control belongs in core affects restore completeness and security; an open closing PR already claims one implementation path.

options.title: Review or replace native exclusions
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/44288 or a narrower replacement to settle smart/custom excludes, protected paths, manifest behavior, docs, and large-state proof.

options.title: Split reliability first
options.body: Fix clear completion/failure/progress behavior separately while leaving native exclude-pattern policy to https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/40786.

options.title: Defer native exclusions
options.body: Keep core backups coarse, document limits and plugin/ClawHub alternatives, and close only if maintainers explicitly accept that boundary.

recommendation.title: Review or replace native exclusions
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/44288 or a narrower replacement to settle smart/custom excludes, protected paths, manifest behavior, docs, and large-state proof.

likelyOwner.reason: `gumadeiras` is the strongest history signal for the original backup CLI contract and adjacent backup helper refactor.
